basic_info.name: dr.consulta (formerly Dr. Consulta / Doutor Consulta)
basic_info.category: Healthcare services platform — affordable primary-care clinic network + telehealth + discount subscription (not a lab chain, not an AI exam interpreter)
basic_info.stage: Growth/scale-up: founded 2011, 15 years operating; post-turnaround (breakeven reached 2025, +22% growth, new CFO André Nesi, Nelson Teich on board); founder Thomaz Srougi moved to chairman, Renato Velloso is CEO; national telehealth expansion and Rio de Janeiro re-entry underway in 2026
basic_info.pricing_model: Pay-per-service with published flat low prices (60-90% below traditional providers): consultations R$45 (GP with subscription) up to R$59-109 (specialists, 2026); telemedicine GP R$39, specialists from R$59. Discount subscription 'assinatura dr.consulta' (administered by Yalo benefits club, explicitly NOT an ANS-registered health plan): annual R$418.80 consultas+exames (12x R$34.90), R$477.60 with odontology (12x R$39.80), odontology-only R$178.90 (12x R$14.90), semiannual R$239.40 (6x R$39.90); B2B 'Empresas' from R$29.90/employee/month (6+ employees); subscription gives 30% off exams, 20% off dental, free GP telemedicine, 15% off prescription drugs at Droga Raia/Drogasil; excludes check-ups, vaccines, surgeries. Check-up packages sold separately (e.g. Cardiac Check-up R$690). Recent price moves: national telehealth subscription launched at R$9.90/month (Dec 2025-2026, 'Netflix of healthcare' positioning); Instagram promo claims 'social price R$25 from the second consultation' [uncertain — promo context unclear]. Historical: SulAmérica co-branded popular plan 'Direto Sampa' (2020); Cuidar.me-linked plans from R$169/month (discontinued 2024).
basic_info.target_user: Uninsured and underinsured low/middle-income patients (Brazilian classes C/D) paying out of pocket; families (holder + up to 4 dependents); small and mid-size companies as B2B benefit buyers; price-sensitive patients who defer care due to cost
basic_info.scale_metrics: 250,000+ medical consultations/month; ~150,000 unique patients/month; 500,000+ people with access to services; 1M+ patients claimed in app listing, ~2.5M patients served historically (figures vary by source/date) [uncertain]; 31+ units in 2 states (SP + RJ since Copacabana unit, March 2026) per official site, while (stale) Google Play listing claims 50+ centers — company had ~50 units pre-pandemic, downsized, now regrowing (R$40M for 5 Rio units in 2026, first inside Supermercado Guanabara; R$7M 'mega unit' in Santo André); one source mentions a Belo Horizonte presence [uncertain]. Revenue R$350M+ (2022); breakeven and +22% growth in 2025; stated goal R$1.5B revenue within 3 years. Funding: ~R$300M+ total — Series D R$170M led by Kamaroopin (Aug 2024), R$125M earlier tranche with IDB Invest (US$10M equity), FINEP R$30M (R$21M loan) for a 'digital health wallet'; R$70M planned AI/data investment. AI agents attributed R$1.2M/month gross operating revenue (2026). Threat assessment: DURABLE — 15 years of brand, physical assets, capital, nursing-led care programs and WhatsApp-native AI ops in exactly Dr. Exame's price band; the R$9.90 national telehealth subscription is an aggressive acquisition funnel.

product.core_features: In-person consultations in 60+ specialties (incl. 10+ pediatric subspecialties, psychology, nutrition); laboratory and imaging exams (~3,000 exam types) collected/performed in own units; odontology (evaluation + 160 procedures); check-up packages (men/women/cardiac); telemedicine (GP video consults without prior scheduling); chronic-condition Health Programs (diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol) with nursing-led follow-up; guaranteed free return visit within 30 days when requested by the doctor; app/web/WhatsApp/phone booking with same-day slots; online payment up to 10x installments; full clinical history in app (prescriptions, exam results, referrals, invoices/receipts); booking 'for you or another person'; B2B corporate subscriptions; discount card incl. pharmacy discounts.
product.signature_differentiator: Vertically integrated affordable care at scale: own clinic network with transparent flat prices 60-90% below market, same-day availability, a promise-backed 'Retorno Garantido' (free return within 30 days), chronic-disease management programs, and operational AI agents running scheduling/triage/follow-up natively on WhatsApp (75% cheaper than human-only structure, R$1.2M/month attributed revenue). No other Brazilian player combines physical primary-care scale + published low prices + WhatsApp-native AI ops + a R$9.90/month national telehealth funnel. Retail-adjacent siting (clinic inside Supermercado Guanabara in Copacabana) extends the access-first signature.
product.lab_data_handling: Exams are ordered by their physicians and collected/performed inside dr.consulta units (~3,000 exam types; lab collection in-house, imaging in selected units); results are delivered to the patient's in-app history ('exam results in the palm of your hand') alongside prescriptions and referrals. Interpretation is NOT self-serve: results are explained during a consultation, with the free 30-day return binding interpretation to an in-network doctor. No external-exam PDF upload, no ingestion of third-party lab results, no AI explanation of results for patients. Retest cadence is physician/check-up-package driven (annual check-ups sold as packages); no home blood-draw chip, CGM or wearable program found [uncertain — cadence/hardware specifics not documented publicly].
product.family_dependents_depth: Subscription covers holder + up to 4 dependents at no extra cost with NO family link required (each identified by own CPF) — broader than family (friends allowed), but it is a billing/discount construct, not a clinical family layer. App allows booking on behalf of another person. Strong pediatric bench (pediatric cardiology, neurology, pneumology, psychiatry, surgery, hematology, allergy, rheumatology, gastro, ophthalmology, endocrinology). No pediatric reference-range handling product, no caregiver mode with delegated clinical views, no hereditary/familial-risk features found.
product.doctor_sharing: They ARE the provider: the patient's own in-network physician reviews exams and issues prescriptions stored in the app; internal EMR shared across their network. No feature found for exporting a consultation brief/SOAP or structured summary to an external (out-of-network) doctor, and no external-doctor portal [uncertain — based on absence in public materials]. The 'guaranteed return' mechanic keeps interpretation inside the network rather than exporting it.
product.action_loop_monetization: The action loop is fully owned — everything after first contact is monetized in-house: retests and annual check-up packages; dental conversion (evaluation included in subscription, 20% off 160 procedures); chronic-condition programs creating consultation cadence; pharmacy discounts (15% at RaiaDrogasil) as benefit glue; telehealth subscription R$9.90/month as cheap acquisition funnel into paid consults/exams; B2B corporate plans from R$29.90/employee; historical insurance adjacency (SulAmérica 'Direto Sampa' 2020; 27.5% stake in operator Cuidar.me with plans from R$169/month — Cuidar.me abruptly shut down in April 2024, beneficiaries migrated to Plena Saúde). No supplements marketplace, no external imaging/MCED marketplace.

technology.ai_approach: Operational/conversational AI, not diagnostic: (1) StaryaAI-built autonomous agents on WhatsApp — 'Veri' (general service/scheduling), 'Gabi' (Health Program enrollment, 30% conversion in 30 days vs 5% goal), 'Lara' (scheduling, 10% conversion in first month); 3M+ messages exchanged, 276k active users, ~75k conversions, +60% WhatsApp sales revenue, 75% cost saving vs equivalent human structure, patient satisfaction 8.2/10 with automated service, internal NPS 95% from nurses freed of repetitive tasks (Exame exclusive, July 2026). (2) Proprietary demand-prediction algorithms sizing capacity and specialty mix (a company staple since the Srougi era). (3) FINEP R$30M program (incl. R$21M loan) for proprietary AI + 'digital health wallet', part of R$70M AI/data investment plan. Human-in-the-loop: nurses and physicians consume agent output; agents do triage/scheduling/follow-up, never diagnosis.
technology.data_inputs: Own EMR (consultations, prescriptions, exam results, referrals), scheduling/CRM and no-show data, chronic-program nursing questionnaires and follow-up interactions, WhatsApp conversation data. No wearable, CGM, genetic or consumer-health-app ingestion found.
technology.data_interoperability: Closed ecosystem: own iOS/Android app + web portal + WhatsApp + phone hotline are the surfaces; exam results live inside their history. No public evidence of FHIR, RNDS/REL, Apple Health Records, Health Connect, or external LIS integration, and no external PDF ingestion for patients [uncertain — absence-based, no public API documentation]. Exhaustion is limited to in-app prescriptions/results/receipts and benefit discounts. WhatsApp is the widest ingestion/engagement surface and effectively their interoperability layer with the patient.
technology.platform: Mobile apps (iOS/Android) + web portal + WhatsApp + phone center, on top of a physical clinic network (31+ units SP/RJ); B2B sales channel for corporate subscriptions.

ux.onboarding: Fast and low-friction: book in minutes via app/site/WhatsApp/phone with same-day slots; CPF-based identification; subscription released immediately after payment (no adhesion fee); online payment up to 10x interest-free installments; telemedicine GP available without prior scheduling for subscribers.
ux.data_visualization: Exam results presented as reports/list inside the clinical history in the app; no trend charts, health scores, or reference-range visualization marketed publicly — the 'visualization' moment is delegated to the consultation with a physician [uncertain — based on absence in public materials].
ux.engagement_channel: WhatsApp-first: AI agents handle scheduling, symptom triage routing and post-care follow-up conversationally (3M+ messages, 276k active users); app + email + content-heavy blog (SEO articles) as secondary channels; retention spine is the chronic-condition Health Programs with nursing touchpoints and the subscription discount economics. Usage pattern remains largely transactional (patients arrive for a consult/exam); Reclame Aqui complaints (scheduling errors, waiting-room delays) reinforce the episodic pattern [uncertain — inference]. No streaks, no community.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Quality institutionalized but young: Qmentum (Accreditation Canada) accreditation IN PROCESS (announced May 2026 — not yet achieved); named responsible technical directors on patient-facing materials (physician CRM and dental CRO); telemedicine under CFM rules; no published accuracy claims or methodology papers (service provider, not an algorithm product — nothing to validate numerically). Trust signals: 8.2/10 satisfaction with AI service (company-reported), Reclame Aqui 7.5/10 'BOM' with 78.7% of 2,580 complaints resolved (recurring themes: appointment not recorded, delays, 'cheap care that turns expensive'). Trust risks: quality-at-cost tension across 31 standardized units; the April 2024 abrupt collapse of partner operator Cuidar.me (dr.consulta held 27.5%) with forced migration of beneficiaries to Plena Saúde — evidence that its regulated-adjacent ventures can fail; nurse-staffed care marketed as differentiator yet automation grows.
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Deliberate positioning outside heavy health-plan regulation: the subscription is an explicit discount/benefits club ('NOT a health plan, no ANS operator registration', administered by third party Yalo) governed by consumer law rather than ANS supervision; the failed Cuidar.me stake (27.5%) was the ANS-regulated experiment that collapsed in 2024. Telemedicine practiced under permanent CFM rules (legal since 2022). AI is framed strictly as administrative/conversational (scheduling, triage routing, follow-up) with no diagnostic claims — therefore no ANVISA SaMD registration (RDC 657/2022) engaged, in contrast to any diagnostic-claiming software. LGPD compliance as health-data controller; explicit disclaimer that it does not provide emergency/urgent care.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: GAPS (Dr. Exame opportunities): no self-serve interpretation of exam results — the 'what do my numbers mean' moment is gated behind a paid consultation and a 30-day return; no external lab-result ingestion (patients cannot upload PDFs from other labs, so nothing to interpret outside their own orders); no trends, scores or range visualization; dependents are a billing construct with no clinical family layer (no pediatric reference handling, no hereditary-risk view, no caregiver clinical mode); no wearable/genetic inputs; physical footprint limited to SP/RJ while the R$9.90 telehealth goes national without exam depth; no structured brief for external doctors. WHAT WORKS (inspiration, not copy): radical price transparency with published flat prices; R$9.90/month national telehealth as acquisition funnel; WhatsApp-native AI operations with measured revenue and 75% cost reduction; 'Retorno Garantido' (free return in 30 days) as a trust-promise; agent-driven chronic-program enrollment (30% conversion); 4 dependents free without family-link requirement; B2B from R$29.90/employee; retail siting (clinic inside a supermarket) for access.
trust_gaps.relevance: HIGH — competes directly for the same price-sensitive Brazilian patient at the exact moment Dr. Exame monetizes: the patient gets cheap labs and consults at dr.consulta, but result interpretation is locked to an in-network paid visit, leaving the instant, longitudinal, family-aware interpretation layer open. Also the benchmark for pricing floor (R$45-109 consults, R$9.90 telehealth) and for WhatsApp-first retention mechanics in Brazilian popular healthcare.
